definition: Lemmatization (or less commonly lemmatisation) in linguistics is the process of grouping together the inflected forms of a word so they can be analysed as a single item, identified by the word's lemma, or dictionary form.
details: In computational linguistics, lemmatization is the algorithmic process of determining the lemma of a word based on its intended meaning. Unlike stemming, lemmatization depends on correctly identifying the intended part of speech and meaning of a word in a sentence, as well as within the larger context surrounding that sentence, such as neighbouring sentences or even an entire document. As a result, developing efficient lemmatization algorithms is an open area of research.

explainer.lead: Lemmatization groups the inflected forms of a word so they can be analyzed as one item, identified by the word's dictionary form (lemma). It matters in computational linguistics because it reduces vocabulary to meaningful base forms.

tiers.eli5: It's treating 'run', 'running' and 'ran' as the same word, so a computer can file them all under one heading.
tiers.practitioner: In computational linguistics it is the algorithmic process of determining a word's lemma from its intended meaning, which requires correctly identifying its part of speech. A pitfall: unlike stemming, it depends on that correct identification and on context, so errors in tagging propagate — and efficient lemmatization algorithms remain an open research area.
tiers.paperLevel: Grouping inflected word forms so they are analyzed as a single item identified by the lemma; unlike stemming it depends on correctly identifying the intended part of speech and meaning, including surrounding context such as neighbouring sentences or the whole document.

explainer.example: Given 'The cats were running', a lemmatizer maps 'cats' to 'cat', 'were' to 'be' and 'running' to 'run', using part-of-speech information rather than suffix stripping.
